rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural عرضهم treats the displayed items as embodied persons; if the names alone were intended, feminine forms would also work, and عرضها could refer to names or embodied figures.
rows.anchor: على مذهب شخوص العالمين وسائر العالم

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud’s reading has the feminine plural عرضهن, consistent with referring to names without their embodied referents.
rows.anchor: هي في حرف عبد الله

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy’s reading has عرضها, which can refer either to the names or to the displayed figures.
rows.anchor: وفي حرف أبي «ثم عرضها»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the hamzated form أنبئهم, hāʾ and mīm cannot take kasra because the trigger is hamza, not yāʾ as in عليهم.
rows.anchor: إن همزت قلت أنبئهم ولم يجز كسر الهاء والميم لأنها همزة وليست بياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the hamza is elided, the pronoun may be raised or kasra-marked, whether the yāʾ is retained or omitted.
rows.anchor: وإن ألقيت الهمزة فأثبت الياء أو لم تثبتها جاز رفع «هم» وكسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فتكونا may be jussive by coordination with the prohibition; this makes it a renewed prohibition, as in Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse.
rows.anchor: وإن شئت عطفته على أول الكلام فكان جزما مثل قول امرئ القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subjunctive parses فتكونا as a consequence or recompense; the same construction appears in three other Qurʾanic prohibitions.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الجواب والنصب لا تفعل هذا فيفعل بك مجازاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafʿ is unavailable for either parse unless the second clause begins a distinct thought, as in the warning that someone will ride back to you.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز الرفع في واحد من الوجهين إلا أن تريد الاستئناف بخلاف المعنيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem ألم تسأل الربع القديم فينطق begins as an expected answer, then the speaker corrects himself; Zuhayr similarly corrects the claim that the old traces remain unchanged.
rows.anchor: كما قال زهير بن أبي سلمى المزني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form ادكروا corresponds to تذكروا elsewhere and to the everyday instruction اذكر مكاني من أبيك.
rows.anchor: ومثله في الكلام أن تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker’s yāʾ has both a still and a vowelled form; before the definite article, Arabs prefer the vowelled form to avoid losing the yāʾ at the article’s initial sukūn.
rows.anchor: فإن كل ياء كانت من المتكلم ففيها لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukūn remains permissible before alif-lām; يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا was read both with a still yāʾ and with its vowelled form.
rows.anchor: وقد يجوز إسكانها عند الألف واللام وقد قال الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the yāʾ is absent, as in فبشر عباد, it cannot be vowelled; this rule applies to comparable Qurʾanic forms.
rows.anchor: فلا تنصب ياؤها وهي محذوفة وعلى هذا يقاس كل ما في القرآن منه

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says Arabs prefer a vowelled yāʾ before any hamza except alif-lām, as in إني أخاف الله; al-Farrāʾ says he did not observe this usage.
rows.anchor: زعم الكسائي أن العرب تستحب نصب الياء عند كل ألف مهموزة سوى الألف واللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ generally heard the yāʾ left still before hamza; he allows vowelled forms in the rare phrases بي أخواك and لي ألفان, while keeping the same underlying analogy.
rows.anchor: عندي أبوك بتحريك الياء إلا أن يتركوا الهمز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When two exchanged goods are not standard money, the price is accusative and the bāʾ marks the merchandise; either item may be treated as price, as in buying cloth for a garment.
rows.anchor: وكل ما كان في القرآن من هذا قد نصب فيه الثمن وأدخلت الباء في المبيع أو المشترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With dirhams or dinars exchanged for goods, bāʾ marks the money because it is always the price; Qurʾanic examples place it before the price or exchanged value.
rows.anchor: فإنك تدخل الباء فيهن مع العروض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Money exchanged for money may take bāʾ on either side because each can function as sale item or price; returning a defective slave yields equivalent coins, unlike a replacement slave girl.
rows.anchor: ثم وجد به عيبا فرده لم يكن له على البائع أن يأخذ ألفه بعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a question followed by a conditional, the answer is an independent declarative clause, while the condition supplies its condition; a response after the conditional may therefore be jussive by position.
rows.anchor: وإذا أجبت الاستفهام بالفاء فنصبت فانصب العطوف، وإن جزمتها فصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فأصدق وأكن, وأكن is jussive by the position of the implied conditional response; nasb is also possible by coordinating with the following clause.
rows.anchor: لأنها في محل جزم إذ كان الفعل إذا وقع موقعها بغير الفاء

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud’s reading is وأكون with wāw, also read by some reciters; al-Farrāʾ accepts it because scribes sometimes omit letters intended in recitation.
rows.anchor: وهي في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ supports omitted written letters being intended in reading by examples where alif or wāw is omitted from the script but supplied in recitation.
rows.anchor: بطرح الألف والقراءة بإثباتها فلهذا جازت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet’s jussive وأستدرج after لعلي can be linked to an implicit fāʾ or read as indicative with sukūn for the sequence of motions.
rows.anchor: إلى موضع الفاء المضمرة في لعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some reciters use jussive in لا يحزنهم while intending rafʿ; in أنلزمكموها, al-Farrāʾ prefers rafʿ over jussive.
rows.anchor: والرفع أحب إلى من الجزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After an affirmative clause, an exception is excluded from the stated action; after a negative clause, the exception asserts that action, explaining how إلا behaves in the example.
rows.anchor: فإن كان ما قبل إلا فاعلا كان الذي بعدها خارجا من الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic can omit the plural wāw, relying on the preceding ḍamma; al-Farrāʾ cites سندع الزبانية, ويدع الإنسان and three poetic examples.
rows.anchor: وقد تسقط العرب الواو وهي واو جماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine yāʾ can likewise be omitted with the preceding kasra as its marker; ʿAntara’s line illustrates this in تكحلي وتخضب.
rows.anchor: يحذفون (ياء التأنيث) وهي دليل على الأنثى اكتفاء بالكسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كما أرسلنا can answer the preceding فاذكروني أذكركم as a fronted response, or attach to أذكركم; the second parse is stronger Arabic and treats the kāf as a sufficient condition.
rows.anchor: لأن الكاف شرط، معناه افعل كما فعلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic normally says شكرت لك and نصحت لك, not direct-object forms; poetry from an unnamed poet and al-Nābigha confirms the idiom.
rows.anchor: ونصحت لك. ولا يقولون: نصحتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ولا تقولوا لمن يقتل في سبيل الله أموات, أموات is nominative with an implicit pronoun (“they are dead”), contrasted with “they are alive”; it cannot be an object of قولوا.
rows.anchor: كقولك: لا تقولوا: هم أموات بل هم أحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasb after قول is possible when the word names the utterance itself, as in قلت خيرا or قلت شرا; raised خير instead denotes a thing rather than speech.
rows.anchor: إنما يجوز النصب فيما قبله القول إذا كان الاسم في معنى قول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matching term in وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها denotes retribution from God, not a deed whose meaning matches the offender’s act.
rows.anchor: وليست من الله على مثل معناها من المسيء لأنها جزاء

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud’s reading adds إلى البيت after العمرة; al-Farrāʾ explains that umrah is completed at the House, whereas hajj includes ʿArafāt and all the rites.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله «وأتموا الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means complete umrah through reaching the House and complete hajj through its furthest rites.
rows.anchor: أتموا العمرة إلى البيت في الحج إلى أقصى مناسكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أحصر applies to an illness or fear that prevents completion without coercion; حصر applies to imprisonment or another coercive restraint.
rows.anchor: العرب تقول للذي يمنعه من الوصول إلى إتمام حجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A coercive restraint may be called أحصر if treated as a blocking condition rather than an agent; illness may be expressed as حصره المرض, so حصرتم can also apply.
rows.anchor: ولو نويت في قهر السلطان أنها علة مانعة ولم تذهب إلى فعل الفاعل جاز لك أن تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description حصورا in the account of John means he is prevented from women by a condition, not imprisoned, supporting the distinction based on the obstacle.
rows.anchor: إنه المحصر عن النساء لأنها علة وليس بمحبوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In فما استيسر من الهدي, ما is nominative because that is the more common Qurʾanic pattern; accusative is also possible by supplying أهدوا.
rows.anchor: في موضع رفع لأن أكثر ما جاء من أشباهه في القرآن مرفوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sacrificial hady here may be a camel, cow, or sheep.
rows.anchor: وتفسير الهدى فى هذا الموضع بدنة أو بقرة أو شاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone unable to find the sacrifice fasts three days, ending with the Day of ʿArafah, with two days in the first ten; the seven are fasted on the return journey or at home.
rows.anchor: واليومان في العشر، فأما السبعة فيصومها إذا رجع في طريقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven is genitive by coordination with the three days; accusative is also allowed by starting a new implied verb.
rows.anchor: «السبعة» فيها الخفض على الاتباع للثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule applies to outsiders rather than Meccans; ذلك is nominative, and على can replace لام in “that is upon outsiders.”
rows.anchor: ذلك لمن كان من الغرباء من غير أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحج أشهر معلومات means the appointed time of hajj spans these months; the noun is nominative as a measure of duration, following Arabic usage for periods.
rows.anchor: البرد شهران، والحر شهران، لا ينصبون لأنه مقدار الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known hajj months are Shawwāl, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and ten days of Dhū al-Ḥijjah; the sacred months are Muḥarram, Rajab, Dhū al-Qaʿdah, and Dhū al-Ḥijjah.
rows.anchor: والأشهر المعلومات شوال وذو القعدة وعشر من ذي الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs call a period months or days even when it includes only part of its final unit; they say two days though the pilgrim hurries in one and a half, and this usage is limited to appointed times.
rows.anchor: وإنما جاز أن يقال له أشهر وإنما هما شهران وعشر من ثالث لأن العرب إذا كان الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing death before Uhud means seeing its causes, such as swords and other weapons.
rows.anchor: وهذا يوم أحد يعني السيف وأشباهه من السلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A question followed by a conditional takes an independent declarative answer; an answer like لا يزل is jussive by position even though semantically raised, as in the quoted poem.
rows.anchor: كل استفهام دخل على جزاء فمعناه أن يكون في جوابه خبر يقوم بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفإن مت فهم الخالدون means “Are they the immortal ones if I die?”; moving إن كفرتم before تتقون likewise permits either rafʿ or jazm.
rows.anchor: ومثله أفإن مت فهم الخالدون المعنى: أنهم الخالدون إن مت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ربيون means thousands.
rows.anchor: والربيون الألوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings قتل and قاتل yield different referents for فما وهنوا: survivors in the passive reading, or the fighters in the active reading.
rows.anchor: فمن أراد قتل جعل قوله: فما وهنوا لما أصابهم للباقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context is Uhud: people said Muhammad had been killed, some failed and some turned hypocrite; the verses then affirmed his mortality and cited earlier prophets with many steadfast followers.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر هذا لانهم قالوا يوم أحد: قتل محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وكأين means كم, “how many.”
rows.anchor:
ومعنى وكأين: وكم.
وقد قال بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes take the prophet as the object of قتل and معه ربيون as “with him were many cohorts”; the followers did not retreat or lose resolve after his death, a reading al-Farrāʾ calls good.
rows.anchor: وقد قال بعض المفسرين: «وكأين من نبي قاتل»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In وما كان قولهم إلا أن قالوا, he parses قول as accusative with kāna and أن as nominative; raising قول and making أن accusative is also correct.
rows.anchor: والوجه أن تجعل (أن) في موضع الرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: واحدة is feminine because نفس is grammatically feminine, though واحد would also be valid by reference to the male, Adam.
rows.anchor: قال (واحدة) لأن النفس مؤنثة، فقال: واحدة لتأنيث النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بث منهما means God spread the creatures; Arabic also uses أبث الله الخلق and both بثثتك and أبثثتك for telling someone what is within oneself.
rows.anchor: العرب تقول: بث الله الخلق: أي نشرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses الأرحام accusatively as an additional object of “fear”: fear God and kinship ties, lest you sever them.
rows.anchor: فنصب الأرحام يريد واتقوا الأرحام أن تقطعوها

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Ibrāhīm read الأرحام in the genitive, comparing بالله والرحم.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش عن إبراهيم أنه خفض الأرحام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ calls the genitive reading awkward because Arabic does not coordinate a genitive already represented by a pronoun; he permits this construction in poetry under metrical constraint.
rows.anchor: وفيه قبح لأن العرب لا ترد مخفوضا على مخفوض وقد كنى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses the genitive construction in نعلق في مثل السواري سيوفنا … والكعب; al-Farrāʾ says poetic constraint licenses it.
rows.anchor: وما بينها والكعب غوط نفانف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some read تسائلون as تتساءلون with the first tāʾ assimilated into the sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم تسائلون به يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not exchange orphan property for your own: their property is forbidden to you while yours is lawful.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا تأكلوا أموال اليتامى بدل أموالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حوبا means a great sin; the Banū Asad also use الحائب for “murderer,” from حاب يحوب.
rows.anchor: ورأيت بني أسد يقولون الحائب: القاتل، وقد حاب يحوب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan read حوبا with the variant vocalization reported here.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن (إنه كان حوبا كبيرا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here اليتامى are the owners of property; the shift to marriage responds to people avoiding shared food with orphans from scruple, so they should also fear marrying multiple women without justice.
rows.anchor: واليتامى في هذا الموضع أصحاب الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation is: if you are scrupulous about eating with orphans, be scrupulous about combining wives without fairness; marry one through four.
rows.anchor: فاحرجوا من جمعكم بين النساء ثم لا تعدلون بينهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما طاب لكم uses ما because the intended sense is the action of choosing what one wants; من would be possible but would mean the person whom one chooses.
rows.anchor: إلى الفعل كما قال أو ما ملكت أيمانكم يريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pre-Islamic son from another wife could claim his deceased father’s widow by throwing his garment over her, without a new dowry, then harm her to seize her inherited property.
rows.anchor: فألقى ثوبه عليها، فتزوجها بغير مهر إلا مهر الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ولا تعضلوهن, the verb is subjunctive under an implied أن; Ibn Masʿud’s reading makes أن explicit, while jussive prohibition is also valid.
rows.anchor: ولا تعضلوهن (تعضلوهن) في موضع نصب بأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أفضى بعضكم إلى بعض means being alone with her, even without intercourse.
rows.anchor: الإفضاء أن يخلو بها وإن لم يجامعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “solemn covenant” is the obligation expressed as either retaining a wife honorably or releasing her kindly.
rows.anchor: الغليظ الذي أخذنه قوله تبارك وتعالى فإمساك بمعروف أو تسريح بإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن تجمعوا بين الأختين is nominative in sense, like the verbal noun الجمع بين الأختين.
rows.anchor: أن في موضع رفع كقولك: والجمع بين الأختين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المحصنات can mean chaste women or married women whom their husbands have protected.
rows.anchor: ذوات الأزواج التي أحصنهن أزواجهن

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: Fatḥ is the more common vocalization of المحصنات; ʿAlqama reports kasr throughout the Qurʾan except here, where it means married captives from enemy territory, lawful after one menstrual period.
rows.anchor: وقد روى علقمة : «المحصنات» بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتاب الله عليكم means a divine prescription binding on you, comparable to كتابا من الله عليكم; he prefers this to some grammarians’ parse عليكم كتاب الله.
rows.anchor: وقد قال بعض أهل النحو: معناه : عليكم كتاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted accusative is uncommon but possible with an implied verb, as illustrated by the poet’s دلوى دونكا; the bucket is also read nominatively like زيد فاضربوه.
rows.anchor: وهو جائز كأنه منصوب بشيء مضمر قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما وراء ذلكم means everything besides the prohibited categories; elsewhere بما وراءه likewise means “besides it.”
rows.anchor: وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن تبتغوا can be nominative as an explanation of ما, genitive by an understood preposition after ما وراء ذلكم, or accusative when the preposition is omitted.
rows.anchor: يكون تفسيرا ل (ما)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: العقود means covenants; the two terms are equivalent.
rows.anchor: يعني: بالعهود. [والعقود] والعهود واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بهيمة الأنعام here means wild cattle, gazelles, and wild asses.
rows.anchor: أحلت لكم بهيمة الأنعام وهي بقر الوحش والظباء والحمر الوحشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلا ما يتلى عليكم may be accusative or nominative as an exception; it means what God explains as forbidden while in consecration or within the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب بالاستثناء، ويجوز الرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غير محلي الصيد means without deeming hunting lawful while consecrated; غير functions like لا, and محلي الصيد would itself be accusative, as in the Ibn Masʿud reading آمي البيت.
rows.anchor: يقول: أحلت لكم هذه غير مستحلين للصيد وأنتم حرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إلى طعام غير ناظرين إناه uses the same construction: the food is permitted without excess or transgression.
rows.anchor: وهو بمنزلة قولك (في قولك) أحل لك هذا الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن الله يحكم ما يريد means He decides whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: ما يريد: يقضى ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Arabs did not regard Ṣafā and Marwa as divine rites and did not circumambulate between them; the command forbids treating that abandonment as permissible.
rows.anchor: ولا يطوفون بينهما، فأنزل الله تبارك وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا الشهر الحرام forbids fighting during the sacred month.
rows.anchor: ولا القتال في الشهر الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا الهدي forbids interfering with the polytheists’ sacrificial camels or frightening anyone who marks a camel; Meccans used tree bark, other Arabs wool or hair.
rows.anchor: أن تعرضوا له ولا أن تخيفوا من قلد بعيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا آمين البيت means do not bar those, including polytheists, who head for the sanctuary; al-Farrāʾ says the command was abrogated by the command in al-Tawbah to kill polytheists wherever found.
rows.anchor: ثم نسخت هذه الآية التي في التوبة فاقتلوا المشركين

rows.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read يجرمنكم with the form from أجرمت; the standard reader form has an opened yāʾ, interpreted as “do not let hatred make you transgress.”
rows.anchor: قرأها يحيى بن وثاب والاعمش: ولا يجرمنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استقسموا means seeking a decision by arrows kept at the Kaʿba, marked “my Lord commands” or “my Lord forbids”; travelers drew one to decide whether to go.
rows.anchor: الاستقسام: أن سهاما كانت تكون في الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause ends at فسق; اليوم is governed by يئس, not by فسق.
rows.anchor: ذلكم فسق اليوم والكلام منقطع عند الفسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In اليوم أحل لكم الطيبات, اليوم is accusative as a temporal adverb attached to أحل.
rows.anchor: اليوم أحل لكم الطيبات نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غير متجانف لإثم means not intending sin, like غير محلي الصيد; غير is a circumstantial accusative describing من and is outside the noun governed by اضطر.
rows.anchor: غير متجانف لإثم مثل قوله غير محلي الصيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الجوارح means dogs; مكلبين is a circumstantial accusative describing the people who own or train dogs, and ما is nominative.
rows.anchor: يعنى الكلاب. ومكلبين نصب على الحال خارجة من (لكم) ، يعني بمكلبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تعلمونهن means training the dogs not to eat their prey.
rows.anchor: وقوله: (تعلمونهن) : تؤدبونهن ألا يأكلن صيدهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only prey held for the owner and not eaten is lawful; if the dog eats it, it held it for itself.
rows.anchor: فكلوا مما أمسكن عليكم مما لم يأكلن منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وأرجلكم is coordinated with الوجوه; al-Farrāʾ reports Ibn Masʿud’s reading with the order moved forward and back.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه قرأ (وأرجلكم) مقدم ومؤخر

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says the revealed text prescribed wiping, while the Prophetic practice prescribed washing.
rows.anchor: عن علي أنه قال: نزل الكتاب بالمسح، والسنة الغسل

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says Gabriel brought the command to wipe to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: نزل جبريل صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمسح على محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ’s conclusion is that the sunnah requires washing.
rows.anchor: على محمد صلى الله عليهما وعلى جميع الأنبياء. قال الفراء: السنة الغسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الغائط is a euphemism for a man’s going into seclusion to relieve himself.
rows.anchor: من الغائط كناية عن خلوة الرجل إذا أراد الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هو refers to the action; without it أقرب would be accusative, as in انتهوا خيرا لكم, and similar constructions use ذلك or ذلكم.
rows.anchor: لو لم تكن (هو) فى الكلام كانت (أقرب) نصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يبين لكم على فترة من الرسل أن تقولوا means He makes it clear so you cannot say no bearer of good news came, paralleling يبين الله لكم أن تضلوا.
rows.anchor: كي لا تقولوا: ما جاءنا من بشير مثل ما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets in جعل فيكم أنبياء are the seventy whom Moses selected to accompany him to the mountain.
rows.anchor: يعني السبعين الذين اختارهم موسى ليذهبوا معه إلى الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وجعلكم ملوكا means each person is a king in his own home because no one enters without permission.
rows.anchor: يقول: أحدكم في بيته ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gifts unavailable to others were shade from white clouds and the manna and quails.
rows.anchor: وآتاكم ما لم يؤت أحدا من العالمين ظللكم بالغمام الابيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Holy Land is said to be Damascus, Palestine, and part of Jordan.
rows.anchor: ذكر أن الأرض المقدسة دمشق وفلسطون وبعض الأردن
